changes.reason: Keep the gauge near the symmetric s/px/py/pz projection, so the minimiser cannot drift into the mirror-breaking sigma–pi hybrid basin it reached after 4000 wandering iterations.

diagnosis: This is graphene: a 2D hexagonal cell with two C atoms 1.4245 Å apart and a 16 Å vacuum. The model uses 8 functions from s,p trial orbitals. Disentanglement converged cleanly (Omega_I = 5.51 Å²), so the chosen subspace is not the problem. The spread minimisation is. It ran its 4000 iterations with steps of about 3e-5 that were not shrinking, and it settled into a gauge that breaks the layer's mirror symmetry. On C#1 the function centres sit 0.35–0.45 Å off the atom, and two of them are displaced out of the plane, to z = +0.44 and z = −0.28 Å. On C#2 there is a pair at z ≈ ±0.46 Å and two wide in-plane functions (1.47 Å², against about 0.6–0.73 Å² for the other six). So the functions are tetrahedral-like hybrids that mix the in-plane bonding states (sigma) with the out-of-plane pz states (pi), and the two atoms are not treated alike. Symmetry keeps sigma and pi bands apart, and they cross. A gauge that mixes them has to change sharply near those crossings. That shows up as interpolation wiggles in a band the frozen window pins. At the mesh points every frozen state is reproduced to about 1e-5 eV. Between them, on the path, occupied band 3 (−10.6 to −3.1 eV) is wrong by up to 1.08 eV near k ≈ (0.35, 0.29). The failure is in the model itself, not in the truncation: eta_2 is 124.9 meV untruncated and 114.1 meV truncated, and only 0.2 % of |H|² lies beyond r_c. A larger iteration budget would only push further into this symmetry-broken basin. The trial projection gauge (s, px, py, pz on each atom) keeps sigma and pi separate, so I am capping the spread minimisation at a few iterations to keep the gauge close to that projected start. The orbital labels this tool allows include no sp2+pz combination (the textbook graphene seed). sp3 would build in exactly the sigma–pi mixing. Limiting the gauge step is therefore the change open to me that targets this problem directly.
